questions.text: Which statement about injurious conduct is source-safe?

options.text: The architect should not knowingly injure falsely or maliciously another architect reputation, prospects, or practice
All criticism is banned even when truthful and constructive
False injury is allowed if it wins a commission
The rule applies only to suppliers

rationale.correct: Section 5-g is limited to knowing, false, or malicious injury.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-g is limited to knowing, false, or malicious injury.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.5; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: Before undertaking a commission previously assigned to another architect, what does Section 5-e require?

options.text: Written notification plus determination that the original employment has terminated and been duly compensated
Only a lower fee proposal
Only a verbal call to the owner
No action if the project is urgent

rationale.correct: Section 5-e requires notice, termination, and compensation resolution.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-e requires notice, termination, and compensation resolution.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.3; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: If a new architect performs renovation while the original mass and design are substantially maintained, what should public claims do?

options.text: Limit the claim to the extent of work done to the structure
Claim complete authorship of the original building
Use an unsupported fixed percentage formula
Avoid notifying the original architect

rationale.correct: Section 5-f supports limiting claims to actual work done.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-f supports limiting claims to actual work done.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.4; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: How should exact percentage-credit questions be handled in Batch 112?

options.text: Rewrite them to the source-supported rule: limit claims to the extent of actual work done
Invent a percentage formula
Use the owner preferred percentage
Delete the previous architect from the scenario

rationale.correct: The checked source gives a qualitative claim-limitation rule, not a formula.
rationale.takeaway: The checked source gives a qualitative claim-limitation rule, not a formula.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.4; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: What does Section 5-c say about commissions still in negotiation with another architect?

options.text: They are protected if known to be previously endowed to another architect
They may always be poached
They belong to suppliers
They eliminate compensation

rationale.correct: Section 5-c covers endowed commissions whether agreed upon or still in negotiation.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-c covers endowed commissions whether agreed upon or still in negotiation.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.4; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: When may an architect pursue a commission previously offered to another architect?

options.text: Only after satisfying the source-supported notice, termination, and compensation conditions
Immediately if the new fee is cheaper
Whenever the owner says not to notify anyone
Only by using paid advertisements

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.1; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: What is the critical difference between notification and the complete Section 5-e obligation?

options.text: Notification is one requirement; the architect must also determine termination and due compensation
Notification alone replaces compensation
Termination is irrelevant
The requirement applies only to contractors

rationale.correct: Section 5-e has more than a notice requirement.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-e has more than a notice requirement.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.3; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: A new architect is hired for additions to a building previously designed by another architect. What is the source-safe first concern?

options.text: Notify the previous architect of the contemplated project
Claim full original authorship
Use a supplier discount
Offer a free preliminary sketch to win the work

rationale.correct: Section 5-f requires notice for additions, rehabilitation, or remodeling.
rationale.takeaway: Section 5-f requires notice for additions, rehabilitation, or remodeling.

questions.code_citation: Code of Ethical Conduct, Article VI, Rule 7.4; RA 9266 Section 23

questions.text: If the original architect has retired, what should this batch avoid claiming without more source?

options.text: Detailed due-diligence mechanics beyond the Section 5-f notice rule
That Section 5-f concerns successor work
That claims should be limited to actual work
That false malicious injury is barred

rationale.correct: The checked source gives the notice rule but not detailed mechanics for retirement or death scenarios.
rationale.takeaway: The checked source gives the notice rule but not detailed mechanics for retirement or death scenarios.

Undercut fee, advertise, sign finished drawings
